events.title: Galileo Forced to Recant
events.description: In Rome, the Holy Office of the Catholic Church forced the astronomer Galileo Galilei to renounce his view that the Earth moves around the Sun. He made the formal recantation after a trial for heresy.
events.significance: The trial became a lasting symbol of the conflict between scientific inquiry and institutional authority.

events.title: U.S. Department of Justice Created
events.description: Congress created the Department of Justice. It was set up to handle the federal government's legal business and to support the Attorney General.
events.significance: The department grew into one of the most powerful law enforcement and legal institutions in the United States.

events.title: George V and Queen Mary Crowned
events.description: King George V and Queen Mary were crowned at Westminster Abbey in London in a grand ceremony. It took place at the height of the British Empire.
events.significance: George V led Britain through World War I and the House of Windsor took its name during his reign.

events.title: Germany Invades the Soviet Union
events.description: Nazi Germany launched Operation Barbarossa, a huge surprise attack along a front stretching across Eastern Europe. It was the largest invasion force in history up to that time.
events.significance: The invasion opened the Eastern Front, where much of World War II's fighting and loss of life took place, and it helped decide the war's outcome.
